A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reinforcement-learning study of optical-fiber coupling. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original laboratory training and fiber-coupling tests, motor characterization, and virtual-testbed experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original laboratory and simulation results and adds misalignment, observation, noise, and simulation-pretraining experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed in-situ SAC/TQC controller retains its four continuous actions, history-based observations, reward function, reset procedure, and goal curriculum. The noisy-simulator and absolute-position variants extend the experimental comparisons without revising that controller.

E1.justification: The optical-fiber-coupling task and physical setup remain. v2 extends coverage to manual misalignment through separate mirrors, shifted Gaussian optima, and simulated motor-noise conditions, without adding another application domain.

E2.justification: The six-algorithm comparison and human expert remain. Figure 14 expands the deployment comparison from three to five variants by adding noisy-simulation training with and without subsequent laboratory training. Figure 10 also adds an absolute-position-aware policy comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantive robustness protocols: 29 manual misalignments, 100 tests per shifted-optimum condition, noise factors 0–3, and a history-length-30 condition. It also replaces raw plotted returns with goal-dependent normalized returns. The main controller hyperparameters and existing training budgets remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of robustness to external misalignment, the tradeoff from observing absolute positions, full-episode observation history, and sensitivity to motor-noise intensity. Appendix D.3 extends the existing pretraining analysis to noisy simulation. Most original tuning analyses are retained and regrouped.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1's Gaussian-fit uncertainty estimates disappear, although the fitted widths remain in Appendix C. v2 gives panel-specific explanations of the existing 2σ bands but omits the named pandas ewm.std calculation. The retained simulation studies still report at least five runs.

E6.justification: New results include manual versus automatic reset success probabilities of 0.86 and 0.90 in v2 Table 3, failure of position-aware policies under shifted optima, and noise-dependent learning curves. Figure 14 newly reports benefits from noisy-simulation pretraining. The headline 90% coupling result remains; rescaled existing returns do not establish performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4 introduces a goal-dependent normalized-return definition, dividing return by the maximum obtainable through first-step success at maximum power. The existing POMDP formulation, observation and reward equations, and Gaussian testbed function remain unchanged; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's explicit claim that comparable RL fiber coupling had not previously been achieved. It strengthens the framing around general beam alignment and transfer through sensor changes. The central claims of direct experimental learning and approximately 90% coupling remain.

C2.justification: v1's broad negative conclusion about simulation pretraining becomes conditional: v2 finds noise-aware pretraining helpful. v2 also explains the accuracy-versus-robustness tradeoff of absolute-position observations and the greater noise sensitivity of demanding goals. The standalone limitations paragraph disappears, although episode dependence and some single-run limitations remain elsewhere.

D1.justification: v2 documents dead-zone noise sampling and shifted-optimum construction. It removes the A100 simulation hardware disclosure, simulation runtime estimates, and aggregate laboratory training time. The RTX 4070 disclosure moves to Appendix A; algorithm hyperparameters, software versions, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mareev et al.'s earlier fiber-coupling work and distinguishes its two-degree-of-freedom discrete control from the present continuous four-degree-of-freedom approach. It revises the description of white-light-continuum work and adds references concerning adaptive optics, curriculum learning, and expert demonstrations.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introduction and conclusion passages are rewritten around in-situ experimental learning. Virtual-testbed results move out of the main results subsection, with insights integrated into Section 4 and details consolidated in Appendix C. v2 also adds a Broader Impact Statement and removes the standalone limitations paragraph.

P2.justification: v2 substantially regroups existing observation and algorithm plots into Figures 10–11, adds the noise plots and manual-reset table, and expands Figure 14. Return axes are rescaled and captions expanded throughout. The original Gaussian-fit table is removed, while the apparatus figure is retained.

improvement.justification: The physical misalignment test and controlled shift/noise analyses substantially strengthen evidence behind v1's largely untested robustness claims (Table 3; Figures 10 and 12). Figure 14 also supports a more nuanced conclusion about simulation pretraining. These gains outweigh the lost runtime and fit-error disclosures and reduced prominence of limitations, although claims about arbitrary drift remain broader than the tested conditions.
